checkpoints: Both services running the OpenTelemetry SDK with correct startup ordering does not guarantee one continuous trace, because instrumentation only patches the specific modules listed in the SDK's `instrumentations` array — a hand-rolled HTTP client outside that list is invisible to it.

Within a single process, trace context flows automatically through the active context, which is why `tracer.startActiveSpan` correctly nests a new span as a child of the inbound request's span without any manual wiring.

Across a network hop between two services, context has no automatic carrier — it must be transmitted explicitly via the `traceparent` header defined by the W3C Trace Context standard, or the receiving service has no way to know a parent trace exists.

A raw `fetch()` call bypasses Node auto-instrumentation entirely unless a matching instrumentation package (such as `@opentelemetry/instrumentation-undici`) is registered in the SDK's `instrumentations` array, so the outbound request leaves with no `traceparent` header attached.

When a downstream service receives a request carrying no `traceparent` header, its SDK cannot extract any parent context and instead starts a brand-new trace with a fresh `traceId`, which is exactly why Jaeger shows two disconnected traces instead of one parent/child tree.

The break happens specifically at the outbound hop, not at either service's own inbound handling — each service being independently 'instrumented' only covers its own inbound requests, not the manually constructed calls it makes to other services.

The fix is either to route the outbound call through an HTTP client that instrumentation already wraps so the header is injected automatically, or, if the client can't be swapped, to manually call `propagation.inject(context.active(), headers)` from `@opentelemetry/api` before the request is sent.

Confirming the fix means re-running the flow and checking Jaeger for a single shared `traceId` across both services, forming one parent/child tree with the downstream hop's duration visible as a nested span on the timeline instead of hiding inside an orphan trace.
